extractive.retention: verbatim: every expected answer appears in the output (grading.answered against the output text)

abstractive.retention: qa: the QA reader answers each question 3 times; a question counts as lost only when at least 2 of the 3 replies miss

not_applicable: a candidate whose output equals its input byte for byte did not run on that payload (under its minimum); the row is reported as n/a, not as a score of 0

timing.shipped_rules: ICompressionPipeline.CompressAsync wall time inside the .NET process, after one warm-up call per payload
timing.kompress_int8: tokenize + ONNX run + decode inside the Python process, model loaded beforehand
timing.rtk_ccr: HTTP round trip through a private rtk-proxy (ccr on) minus the median round trip through a second private rtk-proxy with --ccr false, same fake upstream

output_counted: compression counts every character the model would see, including rtk's preview wrapper and marker

amendments.relaxed_view: a second score, score_relaxed, with its own answer count answers_relaxed. Answers are graded by fact (grading.same_fact): both sides are rewritten to one spelling first, so a unit written short (4.2s for 4.2 seconds), a count written number first (7 failed for failed: 7), passed for succeeded, errors for Error(s) and a position with spaces still count. Then the same harmonic mean at the 1 s budget, zero when fact-graded retention is under 0.7, otherwise multiplied by that retention so a lossless candidate stays ahead of a lossy one at equal compression and latency. The verbatim floor-1.0 score stays the headline. Recorded replies are re-graded; nothing is re-run.

amendments.after: amendment 4's fact-graded relaxed view had been seen; the judge had not run
amendments.reason: the owner chose a reader judge for facts the spelling rules cannot recover, such as '2 errors' answered UNKNOWN
amendments.judge: judge_runner.py: for every answer fact grading still calls lost, the QA reader gets the candidate's output and numbered items (question plus proposed answer) and replies yes or no, three times; two yes accept the answer. Accepted answers count in the relaxed view only, never in the headline.
amendments.decoys: every judged answer with a number is also asked with its last number raised by one, shuffled in by a seed fixed per candidate run. If the judge accepts more than 10% of decoys, the judge is not used and the relaxed view is graded by fact only.
amendments.control: summarizer_control losses are judged too; the share it accepts is reported as the judge's leniency
